ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows triangle RST, with a right-angle mark at vertex S; side RS is labeled 25, side RT is labeled 30, and what is asked for is the angle at vertex T. Reasoning: Because S is a right angle, RT is the hypotenuse. For angle T, the opposite side is RS and the hypotenuse is RT, so sin(T) = RS/RT = 25/30. Calculate T = arcsin(25/30) ≈ 56.4427°, rounded to the nearest tenth as 56.4°.

raw_record.question_text: Find the measure of $\angle T$ to the nearest tenth.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as triangle RST with a right-angle marker at S, side RS labeled 25, and side RT labeled 30. Since the right angle is at S, RT is the hypotenuse. The requested angle is at T, and the side opposite angle T is RS. Use the sine ratio in a right triangle: sin(T) = opposite/hypotenuse = 25/30. Then compute T = arcsin(25/30) and round to the nearest tenth, giving 56.4 degrees.
